title: Routing cache stale policy led to cross-region fallthrough and wrong-model misroutes
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Multiple customers reported that production requests were routed to a remote region and an incompatible model variant after a policy rollout, causing increased error rates and degraded outputs. Investigation traced the problem to a stale in-memory routing policy cache in the policy-sync service that allowed a transient fallback to a lower-tier region/model during capacity flaps. This ticket captures the escalation, mitigation, fix, and follow-up actions.
reproduction_steps: Deploy a routing policy update that changes preferred region from eu-west-1 to eu-central-1 for a tenant with a multi-tier fallback policy
Simulate a dedicated capacity saturation event that triggers fallback logic
Observe policy-sync service holding a stale policy version due to race between config write and cache invalidation TTL
Validate that routing decision falls through to cross-region tier and selects an incompatible model variant (model-onnx-v1 vs model-quant-v2), producing errors or poor outputs
timeline: 2026-02-18 09:12 UTC - Customer A filed an incident: requests suddenly routed to us-east-2 and responses had format errors
2026-02-18 10:05 UTC - Pager triggered; on-call triaged to smart-routing team
2026-02-18 11:30 UTC - Identified simultaneous policy rollout and capacity spike in dedicated pool as correlated events
2026-02-18 13:00 UTC - Temporary mitigation: added short-lived tenant-specific override rule steering traffic to eu-central-1
2026-02-19 02:00 UTC - Root cause confirmed: policy-sync cache TTL + race during write meant some instances used stale policy until TTL expired
2026-02-20 16:40 UTC - Hotfix PR merged: explicit invalidation on config write and added strict consistency check during fallback decision
2026-02-21 01:10 UTC - Hotfix deployed to hosted control plane + dedicated control plane; monitoring shows errors dropped to baseline
2026-03-09 15:30 UTC - Postmortem notes finalized and follow-ups scheduled
root_cause: policy-sync service used an in-memory TTL cache for routing policy versions. During concurrent policy write + capacity-triggered fallback events, some routing agents continued making decisions with the old policy because cache invalidation relied solely on TTL expiry instead of an immediate invalidation notification. That stale policy allowed fallthrough logic to select a cross-region fallback tier and an incompatible model variant.
mitigation: Immediate: tenant-specific override to force correct region routing until hotfix could be deployed
Short-term: restart affected policy-sync replicas to flush caches for impacted control planes
Hotfix: change cache invalidation to event-driven (on config write) and add a policy-version check during routing decision to reject stale versions
Monitoring: add metric for policy-version-mismatch and alert when routing decision uses version older than N minutes
resolution: Hotfix (PR #7827) implemented explicit invalidation on policy write and added a version-check guard in the routing path. Hotfix deployed to hosted and dedicated control planes on 2026-02-21. Customers' traffic returned to normal; no further misroutes observed. A follow-up change to sync private deployments is scheduled.
qa_steps: Deploy canary with policy-change simulation and synthetic capacity spike; verify no cross-region fallthrough occurs
Run integration test matrix covering hosted/dedicated/private policy propagation paths
Verify that policy-version-mismatch metric emits and alerts correctly under simulated stale-state conditions
notes: Trade-off considered: switching to strictly synchronous policy writes for all replicas would remove race but add write latency and reduce scalability; we opted for event-driven invalidation plus a lightweight version guard to keep performance impact minimal.
Design review requested from infra and runtime teams to ensure the invalidation mechanism will scale to 10k tenants.
Follow-up tasks: schedule ENG-40405 to roll hotfix into private on-prem updater; ENG-40412 to add e2e test in chaos harness that reproduces policy write + capacity-flap races.
